text:
ben_runtime: ran a few nsys + perfetto traces on the KV cache hot path with seq_len=8192 and were seeing sustained HBM traffic >> everything else. timeline shows big memcpy spikes and repeated small kernel launches that look like cache thrash. link: https://perf.redwood/profiles/1763254800 :eyes:
profiler_bot: nsys summary: GPU HBM read ~640 GB/s peak, avg ~420 GB/s, L2 bw high, SM utilization ~65%, many small kernels (attention_kfwd, kv_scatter, gather_kv) dominating time.
nana_ml: @ben_runtime can you paste the nsys kernel timeline snippet? also which kernel variants were selected (fused vs unfused)?
ben_runtime: pasted snippet below:
```
[ 0.00s ] attention_fwd_fused (kernel)  12.4ms
[ 0.02s ] kv_scatter_small (kernel)    3.1ms
[ 0.03s ] kv_gather (kernel)           2.8ms
[ 0.04s ] memcpy H2D                   1.2ms
[ 0.045s] attention_fwd_unfused        9.7ms
[ 0.055s] kv_write_unaligned           4.0ms
```
Looks like runtime picks fused variant sometimes, falls back to unfused for longer contexts -> extra copies and small kernels.
jess_ops: hypothesis: large seqs cause the KV cache to do many fragmented writes/reads, thrashing L2/HBM. Combined with batching we get many concurrent small kernels -> kernel launch overhead + PCIe/DRAM pressure.
nana_ml: agrees. A few quick experiments: (1) force fused kernels for long contexts and compare; (2) pin KV cache buffers to reduce scatter cost; (3) run nvprof with memcopy breakdown and per-kernel achieved bw counters. commands:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=kv_hbm --sample=none --force-overwrite --duration=30 --process=./serve_bin
nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,dram_read_throughput,dram_write_throughput --kernels "kv_*|attention*" -- ./serve_bin --seq=8192
```
ben_runtime: ran option (1) by forcing kernel selection to fused for the attention path. Result: total p99 latency dropped 18%, HBM peak down to ~520 GB/s, SM util unchanged but fewer memcpy spikes. good sign.
jess_ops: nice. That suggests fallback to unfused is expensive. Next: try adjusting batching heuristic to prefer lower concurrent batches for long sequences (so we avoid many small KV ops overlapping). can we add a runtime switch to cap concurrent requests by seq_len?
ben_runtime: i pushed a quick flag --max-concurrent-long-seq=4 on the dev branch and re-profiled: reduces small kernel overlap, latency slightly higher for single requests but overall tail improved and HBM avg down ~15%.
nana_ml: still worried about L2 cache eviction pattern. perfetto shows repeated L2 miss bursts aligned with kv_write_unaligned. maybe we need tiled writes or an explicit prefetch to keep contiguous blocks.
jess_ops: propose two fixes: (A) update kernel selection policy: prefer fused variants when seq_len > threshold OR when estimated KV touch fraction > 0.6; (B) implement a KV write coalescer on the host that reorders writes into larger contiguous HBM ops.
ben_runtime: agree. I can prototype A quickly. For B we need a short design doc. jess_ops can you draft the coalescer idea? assign to you. :thumbsup:
jess_ops: will draft. quick note: watch out for memory growth when coalescing — use bounded buffer and backpressure. also add NVTX markers around coalescer to measure effect.
nana_ml: one more diagnostic: run the hardware counters for L2 read/write bandwidth and DRAM replay counters. use nsight compute or rocprof (if AMD). we want to confirm replay due to unaligned accesses.
ben_runtime: logging next steps: 1) prototype policy change to prefer fused kernels (me) 2) jess to write coalescer spec and perf test plan 3) ana to run detailed hw counters and perfetto traces for tiled vs unaligned write patterns. I'll attach the nsys / perfetto profiles to the ticket.
profiler_bot: attached profiles: https://perf.redwood/profiles/1763254800/nvprof.csv, https://perf.redwood/perfetto/1763254800/trace.pb
ana_ml: thanks. if the kernel selection change looks good we should roll to a canary on Dedicated for a small subset of customers and monitor HBM usage/latency metrics in Console. add rollout + rollback plan.
ben_runtime: will add canary config to the rollout plan. cc @product for SLA implications.
jess_ops: small follow-up question: any relation to quantization paths? could int8 kernels be doing different memory patterns?
ben_runtime: good point — fused int8 kernel exists but we did these runs in fp16. I'll run a quick int8 NVPROF later to compare.
nana_ml: cool. that's it for now. :rocket:
